We're officially putting the call out for speakers, podcast guests and contributors for our 2027 Women in Safety program! And I want to make something really clear...You dont need to be a professional speaker to have something worth saying. Some of the most valuable conversations I've had this year havent been with people holding impressive titles or standing on stages. They've been with people doing the work. People questioning why we do things the way we do. People navigating difficult conversations, challenging traditional thinking, trying new approaches, making mistakes, learning and sharing what theyve discovered along the way. Those are the voices I want to hear more of in 2027. Were building a program that explores the realities of workplace health and safety, including: 🟠 Leadership, influence and trust 🟠 Psychological safety and wellbeing 🟠 Safety culture and organisational change 🟠 Work as imagined vs work as done 🟠 Safety vs productivity 🟠 Career confidence and professional development 🟠 Moving beyond complianceAnd there are plenty of ways to get involved! 🎙️ Women in Safety Podcast — share your experiences, insights and perspectives through genuine conversations. 💬 WiS Exchanges — contribute to facilitated discussions that challenge thinking and encourage connection. 👥 Leadership Exchanges — explore the decisions, behaviours and challenges shaping our workplaces. 💡 Member Workshops — share practical knowledge, tools and approaches that others can take back into their workplaces. You dont need 20 years of experience. You dont need a senior leadership title. And you certainly dont need to have all the answers. You just need something worth contributing to the conversation. Whether youre an emerging professional, experienced practitioner, leader, researcher or someone with a completely different perspective, Id love to hear from you. And if theres someone you think we should be hearing from, nominate them! Our 2027 Speaker Guest Expressions of Interest are now open. 👉 https://lnkd.in/gMtdtJpk Because the future of safety shouldnt be shaped by the same voices having the same conversations. Lets make room for some new ones. 🧡#WomenInSafety #WomenInLeadership #SafetyLeadership #WorkplaceSafety #WHS #SafetyCulture #PodcastGuests

I'm a journalist working on a story for KFF Health News about how emergency medical services are becoming an increasingly important part of health care in rural communities. As hospitals and medical services become harder to access in some areas, paramedics and ambulance crews are often among the first people residents turn to for help. In some communities, EMS providers are also taking on new responsibilities, including helping patients receive care outside traditional hospital settings. I'm hoping to speak with people in rural Arkansas who have experienced these challenges firsthand. Maybe you've had to wait a long time for an ambulance, traveled a significant distance to reach a hospital, relied on paramedics when other medical care wasn't available, or experienced firsthand how important your local EMS crew is to your community. I'm interested in hearing both positive and difficult experiences, particularly from people who have struggled to access medical care close to home. If this sounds like you or someone you know, I'd love to talk. KFF Health News

We asked our CHStoday BizBrief readers, and they had plenty to say. A few numbers that stood out to me: 📊92%of respondents are working parents, but only20%said their employer offers child care benefits. 📊85%said child care has influenced whether theyve applied for or accepted a job. One parent told us child care costs “significantly more than our mortgage.” Others shared how flexible schedules, remote work, and understanding employers have made all the difference. As Charleston continues to grow, I think these conversations are especially important, not just for parents, but for the businesses trying to attract and keep good employees. A big thank-you to everyone who took the time to share their experiences! cpa-firm-partners-what-you-wish-youd-kno.core: Posted in last 7 days CPA Firm Partners - What You Wish You'd Known On Making Partner Making partner at a CPA firm is a huge milestone. It’s also a transition that a lot of people walk into without a clear picture of what’s ahead. Over the coming months I’m going to be creating content focused on what partners wish they’d known when they first stepped into the role. My hope is that it helps new and soon-to-be partners walk in with clearer expectations and adds a little more transparency to a process that often feels like a black box. To make this as useful as possible, I want to hear directly from the people who’ve lived it: If you’re a partner, what do you wish you’d known before you made the jump? What surprised you most in your first few years? Compensation, capital contributions, business development, leading people, the shift from doing the work to owning the relationships. Anything goes. Share in the comments or send me a message if you’d rather keep it private. I may feature some responses (anonymously unless you tell me otherwise).

renters-in-ireland-rental-crisis-experie.author: Sweet-Commercial8414
renters-in-ireland-rental-crisis-experie.core: Posted in last 7 days Renters in Ireland - Rental Crisis Experiences Looking to speak to people affected by Ireland's rental crisis for an investigation piece Hi everyone! I’m a journalist currently working on an investigation into Ireland’s “rental rat race” and the experiences of people trying to find and maintain a home in the current rental market. I’ve already spoken to tenants, landlords and homelessness charities, but I’d really like to hear from people who have experienced the rental market first-hand and feel they have a story to tell. I’d particularly love to hear from anyone who has: Struggled to secure a rental despite applying for numerous properties Experienced particularly difficult or unfair treatment from a landlord or letting agent Been asked to pay an extremely high rent for a property that was in poor condition Felt exploited by the rental market Had to leave a home or move repeatedly because of rising rents Ended up homeless or at risk of homelessness because they couldn’t secure or afford a rental Experienced anything else you feel highlights the reality of renting in Ireland today I’m very open to different experiences and perspectives, I’m interested in hearing the stories that don’t always get told. If you’d be comfortable speaking to me, please feel free tosend me a DMand we can have a chat about the investigation and take it from there. I’m happy to explain more about who I am and what the piece is for before you decide whether you’d like to participate. Thanks so much!
